name_reason: Follows the DPMI wrapper convention fd2_dpmi_*; descriptor 'unlock_region' accurately reflects DPMI INT 31h fn 0x601 (Unlock Linear Region). No Ghidra address residue in the name. Mirror of fd2_dpmi_lock_region (fn 0x600).
purpose: Wrapper for DPMI INT 31h function 0x601 (Unlock Linear Region): unlocks a linear memory region so its pages may be paged out again.
logic_summary: Takes two linear byte addresses; normalizes them so base = min(a,b) and size = max(a,b) - base + 1 (order-independent). Packs base into BX:CX (high16:low16) and size into SI:DI, sets EAX = 0x601, calls int386(0x31, &in_r, &out_r), and returns 1 when the carry flag is clear (success), 0 otherwise. Functionally identical to fd2_dpmi_lock_region except the DPMI function number is 0x601 (unlock) instead of 0x600 (lock). In the original binary the two share an INT 31h dispatch tail (this body JMPs into fd2_dpmi_lock_region at 0x362a7); the C source models it as a self-contained, functionally-equivalent function.

params.name: param_1
params.semantics: One endpoint (start or end) of the linear byte-address range to unlock; auto-swapped with param_2 so argument order does not matter. Src names this page_start (uint32), though per the documented caveat on fd2_dpmi_lock_region these are raw linear byte addresses, not page numbers.
params.reason: param_1 is a generic placeholder; rename to match the src identifier and the sibling fd2_dpmi_lock_region for cross-file consistency. Records proposal only; Stage 2 applies.

params.name: param_2
params.semantics: The other endpoint of the linear byte-address range; auto-swapped with param_1. Src names this page_end (uint32); like param_1 it is a raw linear byte address per the documented caveat on fd2_dpmi_lock_region.
params.reason: param_2 is a generic placeholder; rename to match the src identifier and the sibling fd2_dpmi_lock_region for cross-file consistency. Records proposal only; Stage 2 applies.

returns.semantics: 1 = success (DPMI host cleared the carry flag), 0 = failure (carry flag set). Derived from out_r.x.cflag == 0.

notes: src comment (dpmi.c lines 106-111) is already concise, accurate, and references fd2_dpmi_lock_region for the shared parameter semantics -- left unchanged. Ghidra plate is more verbose (includes disassembly-level detail and the shared-tail/JMP-to-0x362a7 layout fact) but is technically accurate and not contradictory/stale, so left unchanged per the 'consistent => do not touch plate' rule. Disassembly confirmed: SUB ESP,0x38; min/max normalize; size=max-min+1; [ESP]=0x601; JMP 0x000362a7 into lock_region's shared INT 31h dispatch tail. The shared-tail JMP is a vendor code-layout fact (lock/unlock share the int386 + CF-check epilogue) and a known Layer-2 functional-equivalence emit pattern, not a logic concern -- no issues raised.
